UK duo Autechre make music in a way that's intuitive and personal, and explores just a small zone of what's currently possible.
One of the duo's working methods has been sending back and forth globs of code created in Max, a visual programming environment for audio, until interesting sounds and music start to develop.

By working with programming, probability, logic, chance operations and the like, the traditional boundaries in electronic music between sound synthesis (making the sounds) and sequencing (organising them) effectively ceases to exist.
Autechre still make dance music, but their rhythms are sometimes a matter of algorithms.
They've talked in the past of how software used in the 2010s on albums such as Oversteps and Exai would be part of their tour set-up.
The way those interfaces are used naturally evolves on the road, and then inevitably feeds back into the creative process of making the next album.
Around the middle of the 2010s, Autechre began to experiment with albums and tracks of long duration.

Like many experimental musicians, the pair have an interest in durational cinema where gradual developments can dovetail and diverge in an almost symphonic way, and they've expressed a particular interest in David Lynch's work.

the name emerged during a creative session on an Atari. The inception of the name was somewhat serendipitous yet intentional. The first two letters, "au", were chosen deliberately to resonate with an 'au' sound present in the track they were working on. Following this initial spark of intention, the other letters in "Autechre" were birthed from randomly bashing the keyboard.
Rob Brown and Sean Booth have always wanted to modify and build their own hardware.
They utilize Cycling 74's Max/MSP software, which allows them to design and implement their own controllers, connections, and sound generators.

They continued to explore and experiment with different bits of kit, often modifying and using them for purposes they weren't intended for. This sheer joy in experimenting with gear is a hallmark of Autechre's technical wizardry.
Their approach to music technology is more than just a tool; it's an intrinsic interest. They delve into the nuances of their tools, exploring their capabilities to the fullest.
